chapters.title: Chapter 2351 Kulas' Rebirth
paragraphs: Before the prepared materials lost their effects, Yuan swiftly started the process of combining them together to craft Kulas' vessel.

When Yuan combined the first materials, a profound ripple appeared, sweeping the entire world. As he continued combining them, the ripple grew stronger, and eventually the entire world began trembling from the immense aura emanating from the vessel.

If Kulas could swallow, he'd be swallowing nervously at this moment, his eyes glued to the process. "This phenomenon! It's as if a treasure is being born!" Yu Ning stopped her cultivation to watch, her pretty face full of awe.
One month... three months... six months...
Half a year passed in the blink of an eye. Yet, Yuan was still nowhere near finished with the vessel.
"Hey, Kulas, I need you to enter the incomplete vessel."
Yuan suddenly said to him.
"What? Now? Even though it's still incomplete?"
"Hurry! I'll explain later!"
Hearing the urgency in Yuan's voice, Kulas entered the incomplete vessel without hesitation, his trust in Yuan evident.
"Wow! This feels amazing!" Kulas' surprised voice resounded a moment later. "If it's already this comfortable, I cannot imagine how much better the complete vessel will feel!"
"Since this vessel is incomparably more durable than the average body, I need you to start forming your shape before it's completed, as it'd be impossible once the vessel finishes and hardens."
"I understand. Then I'll start forming my body now."

Soon, limbs began to sprout from the incomplete vessel, but at a far slower pace than when Yu Ning formed her body. In fact, the process was so gradual it resembled the growth of a plant, so slow that it appeared motionless even when watched for a long time.
Days passed. Then weeks. Then months.
After unceasing effort from both Yuan and Kulas, the vessel was finally finished.
"HAHAHA! I AM FINALLY REBORN!" Kulas bellowed, standing tall in a dominant pose as he stood completely naked, proudly displaying his perfectly refined body to the empty world.

Despite his ancient age, Kulas chose the appearance of a young man, with short golden hair, resembling how he looked when he first met Yuan. He was tall, with a lean yet slightly larger-than-average physique—a stark contrast to his days as the Giant Emperor, when his body had been as massive as a mountain and bulging with muscle.
"Put this on," Yuan said as he tossed a pair of white robes at Kulas.

As Kulas adjusted his appearance, Yuan said, "Because you remained in soul form for so long—and considering everything that happened—your entire cultivation base is gone. However, your new vessel is powerful enough to contend with Immortals on its own, so you won't be completely helpless."
"Is that so? I want to test the limits of my new body, so if you don't mind, spar with me."
"Why am I not surprised that's the first thing you want to do after regaining a new body after countless years?" Yuan remarked with a smile.
"I've been without a body and unable to stretch for far too long, after all."
"I can give you a few days to adjust to your body if you—" Yuan had to stop his speech midway when Kulas abruptly lunged his fists at him.
Despite the sudden ambush, Yuan blocked Kulas effortlessly, even catching his fist mid-strike.
Without pause, Kulas hurled his other hand forward. Yuan caught it as well, but this blow was noticeably stronger than the first.
Kulas immediately launched himself off the ground and dropped-kicked into Yuan's stomach.
Yuan absorbed the strike without flinching. He barely felt the impact, but the sheer force still forced him back a single step.

Kulas continued his relentless assault for several days, never once pausing to catch his breath. Yuan spent the first day on the defensive, letting Kulas grow accustomed to his new body. After that, he began to fight back.
Despite having no cultivation at all, Kulas's strikes continued to intensify, each blow fiercer than the last, as though his power were being drawn from thin air.
"Hahaha! This is it! I finally feel alive again!" Kulas laughed with excitement.
A week later, Kulas finally stopped.
"Although I am not satisfied with this little amount of warm-up, I'll end it here," he said.
Yuan nodded and then asked, "What about your cultivation technique?"
Kulas fell silent to ponder for a moment before responding, "I am considering training Great Mammoth Body Refinement again."
Yuan raised an eyebrow at his answer.
"Even after everything you went through because of that technique?"
"It's the strongest technique I know, and I have already mastered it. Moveover, I have no intention of giving up the path of a body refiner, either," he explained.
"The Great Mammoth Body Refinement technique may be powerful, but it's no longer the strongest technique out there. And since you already mastered it, you can simply learn and master another one."

Kulas pondered for another moment before nodding, "You're right. Since I already mastered it, there's no reason not to try out other techniques, especially if they're better. And if anything goes wrong, I can always just go back to my original technique."
Yuan then said, "I don't have any body refining techniques better than the Great Mammoth Body Refinement technique at hand, but I'll help you find one."
"Thanks, brother."
Suddenly, an unfamiliar voice resounded.
"I was wondering why this place smelled so bad despite my frequent cleaning," the voice said coldly. "Turns out someone brought trash home."
"Who?!"

Both Yuan and Kulas were startled by the new voice, even shocked, as neither had been able to sense their presence until they spoke aloud. Hell, even now, they couldn't sense them and had to follow the sound of their voice to locate them.
When they turned their heads and saw a slender figure slowly approaching them from afar, their eyes widened with disbelief.
"Y-You! You're still alive?!" Kulas cried out, his voice trembling with shock.
Yuan also recognized their face instantly and swallowed nervously before muttering in a dazed voice, "Ren Xia?"

chapters.title: Chapter 2352 Indestructible Flesh Forging Scripture
paragraphs: Yuan and Kulas watched with wide eyes as Ren Xia approached them with calm, graceful steps. She was tall and slender, her light pink hair reminiscent of cherry blossoms, her figure refined and well-proportioned, like an hourglass.

A faint frown creased Ren Xia's beautiful face, one that rivaled even Yu Ning, renowned as one of the greatest beauties in the Nine Heavens, and she spoke, "What's with that reaction? You look like you're staring at a ghost."
"If you're alive, why would it be strange for me to be alive as well?"
Before they could respond, Ren Xia turned to look at Yuan and continued, "For you to be surprised as well, I guess you haven't fully recovered your memories yet, my dear."
"Unfortunately, I only remember up to when I defeated Kulas during my life as Tian Yang," he replied with an apologetic smile.
"Sorry."
Ren Xia silently stared at him for a good moment before releasing a deep sigh.
"It's not like this is the first time I've been through this," she then said.
"Why don't you just tell him?" Kulas asked.
"You're just as clueless, huh?" Ren Xia shook her head at Kulas.

She proceeded to explain, "To keep it brief and simple, those who are powerful enough to control their own fate could alter others' fate in unexpected ways. You know the saying, let fate take its course? I could alter that course for him if I interfere too much." "I still don't get it." Kulas shook his head.
Ren Xia rubbed her eyes and sighed.
"He will naturally recover his memories even if I don't do anything because that's his fate. However, if I intervene and help him remember much earlier than he was fated to, it would alter his fate."
Hearing this explanation, Kulas finally understood the situation. However, he still had questions.

"I understand that it might alter his future, but is that really such a bad thing? Only the truly powerful take control of their own fate, and knowing my brother, he's definitely strong enough to do that, so couldn't he just fix his own fate if it goes awry?

"Of course, he can. However, look at him right now. Only those who become a Cultivation God can possibly control their own fate, and he's not even in the God Ascension Realm. Even if he has the potential to reach that level, it might already be too late by then."

"For example, his fate is altered so much that he perishes before reaching Cultivation God, or something happens and prevents him from reaching that level. There are too many variables, so it's best to avoid them altogether by being careful."
"Anyway, I have said enough. If you still don't understand it, you're a lost cause."
Kulas shook his head, a bittersweet smile tugging at his lips.

"You surviving so many eras is impressive," he remarked. "But what really amazes me is how your nasty attitude managed to last just as long." "Oh? You think my attitude is nasty now? Let me show you just how nasty I can be!" Without warning, Ren Xia lunged at Kulas. Before he could even react, her hands had already clamped around his neck. Instinctively, he struck at her arm in an attempt to break free—but the moment his blow landed, it felt as though he had hit solid metal.
"When did you become a body refiner?!" he exclaimed in shock.
"Do you have any idea how long I have been alive? With how much time I have, it's only natural for me to try out different things!" Ren Xia explained as she casually tossed Kulas into the air.
"At my current level, I dare say that I have long surpassed your peak, Kulas!"
Kulas tried to stabilize himself in the air, but he found it impossible, as Ren Xia had enveloped his body with her Celestial Qi.
"Damn it! Why do you hate me so much?!" Kulas cried out loud. "I don't remember offending you to such an extent!"
"Hate you? I don't hate you," Ren Xia replied in a calm voice.
"Bullshit! If you didn't hate me, why are you always trying to argue with me?! Are you seriously that jealous of my brotherly bond with Tian Yang?! Or perhaps, you actually like me—"
BOOM!
As if a mountain had been dropped onto him, Kulas suddenly fell from the sky and slammed into the ground without mercy.

"I mess with you because my dear is too kind to lecture you. Despite all your foolishness in the past, he'd never once complained about your pain in the ass, and you're taking his kindness for granted—at least that's how it looks to me." Kulas tried pushing himself off the ground, but Ren Xia's pressure was too overbearing for someone without cultivation like him.
"T-This pressure... You're a Cultivation God!" Kulas muttered with gritted teeth.

Despite his loud voice, he wasn't actually surprised by this. He continued, "I know how much trouble I've caused you and my brother. That's why I am going to spend the rest of this life that he granted me to repay you two... if you give me the chance!"
Ren Xia suddenly released her pressure on him.
"Your words mean nothing in your current state," she sneered. "Forget repaying us. You can't even protect yourself the way you are now."
"T-That's why I will train hard to—"
Ren Xia suddenly flicked her sleeves, throwing a manual directly into Kulas' face.
Kulas subconsciously caught the manual and read the title on the cover.
"Indestructible Flesh Forging Scripture?"

"It's one of the strongest body tempering techniques in the world right now. It was created by the Indestructible Titan, who is known as the most powerful body refiner to exist. Of course, not even the Great Mammoth Body Refinement technique could compare to it."
Kulas stared at her, his eyes and mouth agape with shock and disbelief.
A moment of silence later, he asked, "Did you acquire this technique specifically for—"
"Don't get full of yourself."
Without hesitation, Ren Xia immediately denied it before he could even finish his sentence, leaving him speechless. Despite all that, Kulas was feeling nothing but delight at this moment.
"Thank you..." he said.

chapters.title: Chapter 2353 Leaving Kulas Behind
paragraphs: "Don't thank me just yet," Ren Xia said to Kulas after hearing his appreciation.
"What?" Kulas raised his eyebrows in a puzzled manner.

A sadistic grin tugged at Ren Xia's face as she responded, "It may be stronger than the Great Mammoth Body Refinement technique, but it is also several times more difficult to cultivate. If you think you had it rough being tortured by the Immortal Clans, just wait until we start training."
A terrified look appeared on Kulas' face after hearing her words, but it was not because he might have to endure unimagine pain. It was simply because he realized that he might be trained by Ren Xia.
"Did I hear you correctly? That you'll train with me? Hell no! I object!" he openly opposed.
Ren Xia sneered and said, "That wasn't a question, so your objection is void."
"Why?! It's not like I am cultivating for the first time! Hell, I am technically older than you! I can train myself just fine!" Kulas remained persistent.
"You're older than me? Don't make me laugh," she sneered with disdain. "You've been dead for most of your soul's lifespan while I have lived all of mine."
"And while you may be able to train yourself, you'll progress much faster if I train you."

"B-But! What about my journey with my brother?! If I train with you, does that mean I won't be able to travel with him?! I have waited so long for this moment! You can't take that away from me! You have no right!" Kulas complained to their parent like a child after being told they couldn't go out to play.
"What?" Ren Xia immediately frowned.

She glared at him and snapped, "You want to travel with him at your current level? How dare you even think such a thing when you've just regained your body and have no cultivation at all! You'd only be a burden to him! Haven't you already caused him enough trouble?"
"T-That's..." Kulas wanted to argue, but he found himself unable to retort, because everything Ren Xia said was true.
While he may have a powerful physique, Yuan was already fighting God Ascension-level cultivators. No matter how powerful his body is, he would never be able to clash with Celestial Qi as a mortal.

"How long do you think it'll take you before you reach a level where you won't be a burden—training alone? Even with your experience, you'd need several thousand years. However, if you train with me, I can guarantee that you'll be somewhat useful in just a few decades."
Hearing her words, Kulas turned to look at Yuan with a reluctant yet pondering face.
Seeing how Kulas was looking at him, Yuan realized what he wanted to say but couldn't and sighed.
"Kulas," Yuan suddenly called out to him.
"Y-Yes?" Kulas' body subconsciously stiffened.

Yuan stared him in the eyes and spoke in a stern voice, "I know what you want me to say. You want me to tell you that it's okay to follow me—that I will be able to protect you. Unfortunately, it's not the cultivators that I am worried about. The Eternals are aware of my return, and I have even attracted the attention of a few new ones."
"No way..." Kulas' jaw dropped.
"I cannot be certain that I will be able to protect myself, much less you. Therefore, you should stay here and train with Ren Xia for now," Yuan said.
"Sorry, Kulas. I know you're disappointed, but this is for the best for both of us."

A bitter smile tugged at Kulas' lips, and he released a saddened sigh, "No, I was being unreasonable to begin with, so there's no need for you to apologize. In fact, I should be the one apologizing to you for trying to push my selfishness onto you even though I was aware that I'd only be a burden."

He clenched his fists and swore, "However, I swear it will not be long! I will train my butt off and quickly follow you, my sworn brother and number one rival, Tian—Yuan!" "Save that enthusiasm for later. You'll need it," Ren Xia interrupted.
"What about you? Aren't you going to spend some time with your beloved?" Kulas suddenly asked her. "I bet it's been a long time since you two met each other."
Ren Xia turned to look at Yuan and smiled, "While it's true that it's been a while, I am satisfied with just seeing you alive and well now, dear. Let's have a proper reunion later."
Yuan nodded, "I'll leave Kulas in your hands."
"Don't worry, I'll discipline him properly," she chuckled with a beautiful smile on her face.
"Oh, right."
Ren Xia suddenly turned to Yu Ning, who was minding her own business nearby.
"What's your name, again?" she asked.
"My name is Yu Ning, Senior Sword Goddess!" Yu Ning respectfully bowed to her.
"Oh? You know me?" "Of course."
"Is that so? Well, I heard what you said earlier, and I am willing to teach you, as well. If you want to serve my husband, you'll need to pass my standards first. What do you say? Are you willing?"
"I-I am willing!" Yu Ning responded after pondering for a brief second. "However, I am an Array Master..."
"So am I," Ren Xia calmly remarked. "In fact, I am a Level 9 Array Master."
"What?! You're a Level 9 Array Master, too?!" Yu Ning exclaimed in shock.
Ren Xia nodded with a nonchalant face, acting like it was only normal for her.
"In that case, I'll be in your care, Senior Sword Goddess!" "Just call me by my name."
"Yes, Senior Ren!"
Some time later, Yuan said, "Since everything is dealt with here, I'll be taking my leave now."
Ren Xia nodded, "Take care, daring. I'll come find you once I am done training them. We have much to talk about."
"See ya later, brother!"

"Until next time, Young Master. Before you leave, I'd like to thank you again for saving me." Yu Ning said as she gave him a deep bow. "If it weren't for you, I'd still be rioting away in the Shadow Realm, after all." Yuan nodded, and after saying his farewells, opened up a portal and disappeared into it.

"Kulas," Yuan suddenly called out to him.
"Y-Yes?" Kulas' body subconsciously stiffened.
Yuan stared him in the eyes and spoke in a stern voice, "I know what you want me to say.
You want me to tell you that it's okay to follow me—that I will be able to protect you.
Unfortunately, it's not the cultivators that I am worried about.
The Eternals are aware of my return, and I have even attracted the attention of a few new ones."
"No way..." Kulas' jaw dropped.
"I cannot be certain that I will be able to protect myself, much less you.
Therefore, you should stay here and train with Ren Xia for now," Yuan said.
"Sorry, Kulas.
I know you're disappointed, but this is for the best for both of us."
A bitter smile tugged at Kulas' lips, and he released a saddened sigh, "No, I was being unreasonable to begin with, so there's no need for you to apologize.
In fact, I should be the one apologizing to you for trying to push my selfishness onto you even though I was aware that I'd only be a burden."
He clenched his fists and swore, "However, I swear it will not be long!
I will train my butt off and quickly follow you, my sworn brother and number one rival, Tian—Yuan!" "Save that enthusiasm for later.
You'll need it," Ren Xia interrupted.
"What about you?
Aren't you going to spend some time with your beloved?" Kulas suddenly asked her.
"I bet it's been a long time since you two met each other."
Ren Xia turned to look at Yuan and smiled, "While it's true that it's been a while, I am satisfied with just seeing you alive and well now, dear.
Let's have a proper reunion later."
Yuan nodded, "I'll leave Kulas in your hands."
"Don't worry, I'll discipline him properly," she chuckled with a beautiful smile on her face.
"Oh, right."
Ren Xia suddenly turned to Yu Ning, who was minding her own business nearby.
"What's your name, again?" she asked.
"My name is Yu Ning, Senior Sword Goddess!" Yu Ning respectfully bowed to her.
"Oh?
You know me?" "Of course."
"Is that so?
Well, I heard what you said earlier, and I am willing to teach you, as well.
If you want to serve my husband, you'll need to pass my standards first.
What do you say?
Are you willing?"
"I-I am willing!" Yu Ning responded after pondering for a brief second.
"However, I am an Array Master..."
"So am I," Ren Xia calmly remarked.
"In fact, I am a Level 9 Array Master."
"What?!
You're a Level 9 Array Master, too?!" Yu Ning exclaimed in shock.
Ren Xia nodded with a nonchalant face, acting like it was only normal for her.
"In that case, I'll be in your care, Senior Sword Goddess!" "Just call me by my name."
"Yes, Senior Ren!"
Some time later, Yuan said, "Since everything is dealt with here, I'll be taking my leave now."
Ren Xia nodded, "Take care, daring.
I'll come find you once I am done training them.
We have much to talk about."
"See ya later, brother!"
"Until next time, Young Master.
Before you leave, I'd like to thank you again for saving me." Yu Ning said as she gave him a deep bow.
"If it weren't for you, I'd still be rioting away in the Shadow Realm, after all." Yuan nodded, and after saying his farewells, opened up a portal and disappeared into it.

chapters.title: Chapter 2354 Family Reunion(End of Giant Emperor Kulas Arc)
paragraphs: After Yuan left, Ren Xia turned to face Yu Ning and said, "Wait here for a bit. I have to take this idiot somewhere."
She gestured at Kulas, who stared at her with a frown.
"You really need to fix how you address me. I was once an Emperor, you kn—"
"Shut up, you big idiot, and follow me."
Without giving him any explanation, Ren Xia turned around and began flying away.
Kulas wanted to rebel and stay behind, but something in his guts warned him that he'd regret it, so he begrudgingly followed her.

However, without any cultivation, he was unable to fly and had to travel on foot. Fortunately, his powerful physique allowed each step to propel him forward like a missile, enabling him to keep up with Ren Xia without too much difficulty.
Of course, Ren Xia could have easily carried him using her spiritual energy, but she decided to let him run instead.
Moreover, Ren Xia's speed would occasionally speed up, forcing Kulas to put in more effort.
"Hey! Where the hell are you taking me in this empty world?!" Kulas asked her after running nonstop for a few hours.
"Empty world? You speak as if you know this place at the back of your hands," Ren Xia sneered. Kulas gritted his teeth and continued following her.
One hour... Six hours... Twelve hours...
In the blink of an eye, the two of them had been traveling for three days without rest. Even for someone like Kulas, he was starting to feel the fatigue.
"You know I just regained my body after spending countless years as a soul, right? How can you make someone like me run like this? You're much more sadistic than before!" Kulas cried out loud.
"Consider this part of your training. A warm-up before the real thing," she calmly replied before going silent again.
After another four days, an entire week since Kulas started running, he started slowing down, and eventually, came to a complete stop.
Seeing this, before Kulas could even complain, Ren Xia spoke, "We can stop here, turn around, and return home to begin your training if that's what you want, but you'll regret not doing this."
Kulas silently glared at Ren Xia, who met his gaze with an uncharacteristically serious expression. He knew she loved to toy with him, but this didn't feel like one of those times.
After a moment of silence, he took a deep breath and, without any words, started running after her again.
Ren Xia didn't say anything either and continued to follow her route.
After nearly another week of traveling, Kulas finally noticed a change in the scenery—the faint outline of buildings rising along the horizon.

At first, he thought Ren Xia had made him run a full lap around the world and was on the verge of bursting in anger. But when he realized there were far more buildings than before, he restrained himself and even picked up his pace.
When he drew close enough to make out figures—silhouettes standing in neat rows, as if waiting for something—Kulas's eyes widened.
'One... two... three...'
He began counting them subconsciously. And when their faces finally came into view, tears streamed down his cheeks.
"Father!" One of these figures cried out loud.

When that familiar voice echoed in Kulas's mind, every trace of fatigue vanished like smoke. His speed exploded in an instant, and he shot forward like a flying sword, arriving before the group of women who were all staring at him with tearful eyes.
"Y-You..."
Kulas was at a loss for words. The women standing before him were none other than his own family—the ones who had chosen to leave the Giant Palace with Tian Yang before he lost control.

"You're all still alive...?" he muttered in a daze, unable to believe his eyes. He had never dared to hope they had survived, and they looked exactly as he remembered, as though the passage of time did not affect them.
"T-This is not an illusion, right? Ren Xia, I swear, if you—"
Kulas was cut off when one of the women suddenly lunged at him, wrapping him in a tight embrace—one so firm and warm that it erased any lingering doubt that they were real.
"Chao Shuying..." Kulas mumbled the name of the woman hugging him, who was none other than one of his wives.
It wasn't long before the others rushed in as well, surrounding him and pulling him into a trembling, tearful group embrace.
After enjoying their reunion, Kulas spoke, asking them in a worried voice, "My rampage during the war didn't affect any of you, right?"
"No, Zaaran's influence couldn't reach us in this place, so we were all unaffected," said Chao Shuying.
"I see... thank the heavens..." Kulas sighed.
He looked at them, tears streaming down his face, and spoke in a trembling voice. "I'm sorry... I'm truly sorry for failing to protect you. I failed as a ruler, as a husband, and as a father."

"Don't shoulder all the blame alone," Chao Shuying said gently, cupping his tear-streaked face with her soft hand. "Every single one of us here has failed in one way or another. What's done is done. All we can do now is move forward—and make sure we don't repeat our mistakes."
Kulas nodded, "I swear that I will protect all of you properly this time."
Once they calmed down, Ren Xia descended before them and said, "Aren't you glad you followed me? Had you given up and returned, you would've left them waiting for you for even longer."
Kulas glared at her. "Why didn't you tell me we were going to meet my family? And what would've happened if I gave up?"

Ren Xia shrugged as though it were none of her concern. "Are you sure you would've preferred that? If I had told you earlier, you would've doubted me the entire way here. Besides, this wasn't my idea—it was theirs."
"And had you given up... you wouldn't have the reunion until after you finished your training," she added with a cold smile.

chapters.title: Chapter 2355 Peak Celestial Qi Comprehension
paragraphs: After letting Kulas spend several days with his family, Ren Xia appeared and said to him, "Let's go. It's time to begin your training."
"Already?! Can't we start later? I've been separated from my family for so long! You cannot separate us again os quickly!" he refuted.
Ren Xia sneered and said, "What happened to your resolution to train as fast as possible from not long ago?"
"T-That's different! I am still going to train hard! Just give me a little more—"
"Kulas, the longer you delay your training, the less effective your training will be," Ren Xia suddenly interrupted, dumbfounding him.
"How does that work?" he tilted his head, looking puzzled.

"Since your vessel is still newly forged, the materials used to craft it remain active. If you train during this period, your growth will be explosive. However, once those materials begin to weaken, the effects will diminish," she explained.
"What?!"
"Just go, my dear." Chao Shuying suddenly said. "We all agreed not to interfere with your recovery, after all."
"But..." Kulas looked at her with reluctance.
"It's not like we'll never see each other again. In fact, you can visit us whenever you have time."
Ren Xia then said, "While it'll be rare, there will definitely be some small breaks throughout your training."
After a moment of silence, Kulas sighed.
He then turned to face Ren Xia and nodded with a resolute face. "Let's begin my training."
"Let's get going."
Without another word, Ren Xia flew back in the direction of her living quarters, where Yu Ning was waiting for their return.

Since he still couldn't fly, Kulas had to run after her again. However, he had much more enthusiasm this time. In fact, his body had already grown slightly stronger from their previous running session.
"See you all later!" Kulas gave his family a swift farewell before chasing after Ren Xia.

Meanwhile, after Yuan stepped through the portal and left his world behind, he found himself drifting within a tunnel of endless void for several days. Normally, teleportation was instantaneous—but for some reason, this passage was taking far longer than it should have.
As he drifted through the void, Yuan pondered his current situation.
"It's been a long while since I've traveled alone..." he muttered.

Although Dragon Goddess Yeyou technically remained within one of his Soul Weapons, this was one of the rare times he was truly alone. Even in his previous lives, he was rarely alone. "Hope the others are doing fine..."
When a few more days had passed, and he was still drifting in the tunnel, Yuan started feeling worried, and he couldn't help but wonder if something was wrong with the teleport he took.
"That world has several entrances and many more exits. Did I take the wrong one by accident? I should've asked Ren Xia before I entered it..." he sighed out loud.

Although he could forcibly tear his way out of the tunnel using Void Manipulation, he was currently traveling through the void at light speed. If he did so, there was a high chance he would emerge somewhere in the boundless Starry Sky without any sense of direction—and becoming lost was the last thing he wanted.
With nothing else to occupy his time, Yuan decided to cultivate. Fortunately, the tunnel was overflowing with Celestial Qi.
He closed his eyes and took a deep breath before attempting to sense the Celestial Qi.
Due to regaining Tian Yang's memories—even reliving his life—Yuan had gained the ability to sense Celestial Qi as natural as breathing.
<Your understanding of Celestial Qi has improved tremendously>
<Your understanding of Celestial Qi has improved tremendously>
<Your understanding of Celestial Qi has reached a new level>
<You have grasped the true essence of Celestial Qi and reached peak comprehension>
It took Yuan less than a day to reach the pinnacle comprehension of Celestial Qi, something that only a few since the beginning of time could achieve after countless years of cultivation.

Even though he could've started cultivating Celestial Qi much earlier, Yuan only started absorbing Celestial Qi once he reached peak mastery. After all, the quality and amount of Celestial Qi one could absorb greatly varied based on their understanding, so the higher one's comprehension, the more effective their cultivation would be.
A vacuum suddenly formed around Yuan, violently drawing in the surrounding Celestial Qi like a whirlpool raging in the heart of a vast ocean.
Yet, when the Celestial Qi entered his body and then his Dantian, they did not push him closer to the God Ascension realm. Instead, it was all being consumed by the Spirit Tree dwelling within.

Realizing this, Yuan didn't panic or mind, allowing the Spirit Tree to consume as much as it wanted. As the Spirit Tree absorbed the Celestial Qi, its radiance grew increasingly pronounced. The entire tree began to glow in shades of blue and violet, an ethereal aurora forming and dancing around it.
Eventually, the Spirit Tree had its full with the Celestial Qi and stopped its feasting.
<The Spirit Tree trembled with excitement as a profound transformation began within it!>
<The Spirit Tree enters hibernation as it begins its evolution!>
[Progress: 1%]
Once the Spirit Tree stopped hogging all of the Celestial Qi, Yuan was finally able to cultivate properly, and very quickly, his Dantian and entire being were overflowing with refined Celestial Qi.
In just a few days, Yuan had accumulated enough Celestial Qi to breakthrough the Immortal Realm and enter the God Ascension Realm. However, there was still one issue—his physique.
"Now... let's see if my physique will allow me to enter the God Ascension Realm, or will it continue to restrict me in the Immortal Realm until I evolve it..."
Yuan took a deep breath and prepared for his breakthrough.
One day... three days... five days later—

Suddenly, Yuan's aura and pressure began to weaken, fading until they were nearly nonexistent. Then his physical body started to blur and grow transparent, as though his very existence were being erased from reality.
Yuan could feel his existence slowly fading, yet he persisted and continued his breakthrough.

chapters.title: Chapter 2356 Yuan's Ascension
paragraphs: As his existence continued to fade, Yuan felt the weight of his body completely vanish, as though he had been severed from it entirely.
Meanwhile, his consciousness—his very soul—felt as though it were drifting higher and higher, as if attempting to ascend toward the heavens themselves.
Although only seconds had passed since Yuan first felt his soul begin to ascend, to him, it felt as though tens of thousands of years had gone by, and he was still ascending.
Despite how long it felt, Yuan didn't panic in the slightest, as he'd gone through this process more than once before.

In what felt like the blink of an eye, a million years passed, and throughout it all, Yuan felt his soul ascending without end. Then, suddenly, he sensed something in the distance—an invisible force. It was boundless, like a colossal wall stretching endlessly in every direction.

This was a phenomenon known as the Celestial Fate, something every Cultivator who has ascended to the God Ascension Realm has experienced. 'Here comes the first layer...' Yuan thought to himself as his soul approached the invisible wall.

Before long, his soul collided with the invisible wall, pressing firmly against its boundless surface. This was the first barrier faced by all who sought ascension. Fail to cross it, and they would remain as a mere Immortal. The trial was simple in concept—yet countless cultivators had attempted it and fallen short.

As for Yuan... his soul easily slipped right through the wall without feeling any resistance at all. To him, it might as well not have existed. After passing the first layer, Yuan's soul continued to drift for another million years until he reached another wall.

Although passing the first layer would qualify one to enter the God Ascension Realm, that was far from the end of the journey. Beyond it lay additional layers, and with each one a cultivator bypassed, their power within the God Ascension Realm would grow increasingly stronger.

The results of this phenomenon varied greatly, shaping the very foundation of one's celestial power. Unfortunately, it was not something that could be controlled. Most could only accept what they were granted—much like their innate talents.
However, those with exceptionally strong Soul Strength—like Yuan—possessed the ability to push themselves beyond their natural limits.
After passing the second layer with the same ease as before, Yuan continued to travel for another million years before reaching the third.
Of course, he also passed that one with ease.
Eventually, he reached the fourth... then the fifth... sixth... each layer requiring a million years to reach, or one minute in reality.

Though reality elapsed slowly, those undergoing the phenomenon experienced that million years in full, and such an immense stretch of time would inevitably erode their mental strength; hence, most stop after the second, third, or fourth layer.

Those who could reach the fifth or sixth layer were considered geniuses, and anyone who surpasses the seventh layer become powerhouses. One minute... ten minutes... a hundred minutes passed in the real world. Yet Yuan remained within the phenomenon, his soul effortlessly bypassing one layer after another.

Thanks to his constantly active soul cultivation technique, his already formidable Soul Strength recovered faster than the phenomenon could exhaust it, so technically, he could last an eternity. However, after the tenth layer, the time required to reach the next layer increased tenfold. Instead of one million years, it would now take ten million years to ascend further.
Therefore, Yuan had been drifting for 900 million years when he reached the 100th layer.
He had expected to pass it as effortlessly as the others. Yet the moment his soul pressed forward, it was pushed back slightly.
For the first time, there was resistance.
Yet, it wasn't strong enough to stop him, and after some effort, Yuan pushed right through the 100th layer.
At this point, the time required to reach the next layer increased tenfold once again. To ascend to the 101st layer, Yuan would need to endure one hundred million years.
Yet despite experiencing a hundred million years within the phenomenon, only an hour would pass in reality.

One might assume that those undergoing ascension could empty their minds and enter a trance-like state to endure the passage of time. Unfortunately, they were required to remain fully conscious and focused throughout the entire ordeal.
A hundred million years... one billion years... ten billion years...
Thanks to the vast experience he had accumulated across multiple lifetimes, Yuan endured the unfathomable passage of time without losing his sanity. Even so, it was far from easy.
After nearly ninety billion years, he barely managed to pass the 999th layer.
Yet the ascent was not over. Without hesitation, Yuan set his sights on the 1,000th layer as time continued to flow.
However, even after a hundred million years had passed, Yuan had not reached the 1,000th layer.
Then a billion years passed.
Nothing.
Ten billion.
He was still drifting.
A hundred billion years later—
Though that possibility was likely, Yuan chose to continue until his mind could endure no more.
And so, time flowed on.
Two hundred billion years later, cracks began to form in his sanity.
After five hundred billion years of drifting through endless void without a single sensation to anchor him, he could feel his mind nearing its limit.
Yet somehow, he endured another five hundred billion years.
Finally, after a full trillion years had passed, Yuan—on the very brink of madness—sensed it.
The 1,000th layer.
Its presence washed over him like a bucket of cold water, instantly clearing the haze threatening to consume him.
The moment he reached the 1,000th layer, Yuan immediately attempted to push through it. However, no matter how much force he exerted, the barrier remained unmoved. He simply could not break through.
'I have no proof... but this is definitely the final layer. And I will break through it at all costs,' Yuan declared inwardly.
With that resolve, he immediately began his second attempt.

sentences.text: As his existence continued to fade, Yuan felt the weight of his body completely vanish, as though he had been severed from it entirely.
Meanwhile, his consciousness—his very soul—felt as though it were drifting higher and higher, as if attempting to ascend toward the heavens themselves.
Although only seconds had passed since Yuan first felt his soul begin to ascend, to him, it felt as though tens of thousands of years had gone by, and he was still ascending.
Despite how long it felt, Yuan didn't panic in the slightest, as he'd gone through this process more than once before.
In what felt like the blink of an eye, a million years passed, and throughout it all, Yuan felt his soul ascending without end.
Then, suddenly, he sensed something in the distance—an invisible force.
It was boundless, like a colossal wall stretching endlessly in every direction.

This was a phenomenon known as the Celestial Fate, something every Cultivator who has ascended to the God Ascension Realm has experienced. 'Here comes the first layer...' Yuan thought to himself as his soul approached the invisible wall.
Before long, his soul collided with the invisible wall, pressing firmly against its boundless surface.
This was the first barrier faced by all who sought ascension.
Fail to cross it, and they would remain as a mere Immortal.
The trial was simple in concept—yet countless cultivators had attempted it and fallen short.
As for Yuan... his soul easily slipped right through the wall without feeling any resistance at all.
To him, it might as well not have existed.
After passing the first layer, Yuan's soul continued to drift for another million years until he reached another wall.
Although passing the first layer would qualify one to enter the God Ascension Realm, that was far from the end of the journey.
Beyond it lay additional layers, and with each one a cultivator bypassed, their power within the God Ascension Realm would grow increasingly stronger.
The results of this phenomenon varied greatly, shaping the very foundation of one's celestial power.
Unfortunately, it was not something that could be controlled.
Most could only accept what they were granted—much like their innate talents.
However, those with exceptionally strong Soul Strength—like Yuan—possessed the ability to push themselves beyond their natural limits.
After passing the second layer with the same ease as before, Yuan continued to travel for another million years before reaching the third.
Of course, he also passed that one with ease.
Eventually, he reached the fourth... then the fifth... sixth... each layer requiring a million years to reach, or one minute in reality.

Though reality elapsed slowly, those undergoing the phenomenon experienced that million years in full, and such an immense stretch of time would inevitably erode their mental strength; hence, most stop after the second, third, or fourth layer.
Those who could reach the fifth or sixth layer were considered geniuses, and anyone who surpasses the seventh layer become powerhouses.
One minute... ten minutes... a hundred minutes passed in the real world.
Yet Yuan remained within the phenomenon, his soul effortlessly bypassing one layer after another.
Thanks to his constantly active soul cultivation technique, his already formidable Soul Strength recovered faster than the phenomenon could exhaust it, so technically, he could last an eternity.
However, after the tenth layer, the time required to reach the next layer increased tenfold.
Instead of one million years, it would now take ten million years to ascend further.
Therefore, Yuan had been drifting for 900 million years when he reached the 100th layer.
He had expected to pass it as effortlessly as the others.
Yet the moment his soul pressed forward, it was pushed back slightly.
For the first time, there was resistance.
Yet, it wasn't strong enough to stop him, and after some effort, Yuan pushed right through the 100th layer.
At this point, the time required to reach the next layer increased tenfold once again.
To ascend to the 101st layer, Yuan would need to endure one hundred million years.
Yet despite experiencing a hundred million years within the phenomenon, only an hour would pass in reality.
One might assume that those undergoing ascension could empty their minds and enter a trance-like state to endure the passage of time.
Unfortunately, they were required to remain fully conscious and focused throughout the entire ordeal.
A hundred million years... one billion years... ten billion years...
Thanks to the vast experience he had accumulated across multiple lifetimes, Yuan endured the unfathomable passage of time without losing his sanity.
Even so, it was far from easy.
After nearly ninety billion years, he barely managed to pass the 999th layer.
Yet the ascent was not over.
Without hesitation, Yuan set his sights on the 1,000th layer as time continued to flow.
However, even after a hundred million years had passed, Yuan had not reached the 1,000th layer.
Then a billion years passed.
Nothing.
Ten billion.
He was still drifting.
A hundred billion years later—
Though that possibility was likely, Yuan chose to continue until his mind could endure no more.
And so, time flowed on.
Two hundred billion years later, cracks began to form in his sanity.
After five hundred billion years of drifting through endless void without a single sensation to anchor him, he could feel his mind nearing its limit.
Yet somehow, he endured another five hundred billion years.
Finally, after a full trillion years had passed, Yuan—on the very brink of madness—sensed it.
The 1,000th layer.
Its presence washed over him like a bucket of cold water, instantly clearing the haze threatening to consume him.
The moment he reached the 1,000th layer, Yuan immediately attempted to push through it.
However, no matter how much force he exerted, the barrier remained unmoved.
He simply could not break through.
'I have no proof... but this is definitely the final layer.
And I will break through it at all costs,' Yuan declared inwardly.
With that resolve, he immediately began his second attempt.

chapters.title: Chapter 2357 Entering the God Ascension Realm
paragraphs: After his first attempt failed, Yuan immediately launched a second assault on the 1,000th layer. Yet the outcome remained the same. If anything, the resistance felt even greater than before.

Realizing brute force would not suffice, Yuan chose a different approach. Stationed before the layer, he no longer needed to focus on advancing toward it, which allowed him to divert most of his attention elsewhere.
Thus, he began cultivating his soul on the spot.
Even so, he could not neglect the ascension entirely, and part of his consciousness still had to remain fixed on the 1,000th layer.
A year... a million years... a billion years...
After cultivating his soul for a billion years, Yuan launched his third attempt.
His soul drove forward with renewed strength, colliding with the 1,000th layer. For the first time, it yielded—warping under the pressure like fabric being forced outward by something beneath it.
However, after a few moments of struggle, Yuan's soul bounced back once again, failing to breakthrough.
"I will not leave this place until I break through—no matter how long it takes!"
Fueled by nothing but sheer determination and stubborn resolve, Yuan resumed cultivating his soul.
Another billion years slipped by in what felt like a blink. Then ten billion. Then a hundred billion—time itself losing meaning as he persisted.
At last, after spending another trillion years cultivating his soul, Yuan made his fourth attempt.
Over that incomprehensible span of time, his Soul Strength had ascended to levels beyond measure—greater than the sum of all his past lives.
"Breakthrough!" Yuan roared as his soul smashed into the 1,000th layer.
The barrier, though thin, held firm for a heartbeat. Then, unable to withstand the pressure, it ruptured as Yuan's soul shot through like a projectile tearing apart a fragile net.
"I did it!" Yuan shouted with excitement.
However, before he could even celebrate, Yuan sensed an indescribable presence descending upon him, forcing his full attention toward it.
What awaited beyond the 1,000th layer left Yuan utterly speechless.

In the boundless void stood a solitary silhouette. Its form was difficult to comprehend, resembling a human figure, yet distinctly not. Within its body flickered countless stars and swirling galaxies, as though the entire universe had been condensed into its frame.
This entity—this existence—exuded a presence that was both familiar and foreign. It carried the aura of an Eternal, yet there was something beyond that... something undeniably superior.
Seeing this existence, Yuan felt a subtle change within him, but he couldn't discern what the change was.
"Are you the Absolute—"
The moment Yuan attempted to speak, an overwhelming force suddenly struck his soul.
His soul was violently repelled, hurled backward through the boundless void at a speed countless times faster than his ascent.
Though it had taken him more than a trillion years to reach that height, he returned to his body in the span of a heartbeat.
<You have transcended the limits of humanity and begun your ascent toward true divinity>
<You have entered the First Level of the God Ascension Realm>
The moment Yuan stepped into the God Ascension Realm, a profound ripple spread across the entire world—one that could only be perceived by those within the same realm.
Its arrival sent shockwaves through their hearts, but this was not the first time they had experienced such a ripple, as every breakthrough into the God Ascension Realm triggered one.
But this... this ripple was on an entirely different level—unfathomably stronger than anything they had ever experienced before.
In fact, the only time they would sense something comparable was when someone reached the very peak of cultivation.
"T-This feeling! The birth of a new Cultivation God?!"
All around the world, experts misinterpreted Yuan's breakthrough. The sheer magnitude of the phenomenon led them to believe that someone had just ascended to the rank of a Cultivation God.
Because of this misunderstanding, many powerful factions dispatched their forces to search for and identify the newly born Cultivation God, unaware that they were chasing nothing but a ghost.

However, unbeknownst to them, before the ripple that shook the Nine Heavens had spread, another ripple had already manifested. And it was unfathomably more powerful—so powerful that it swept across the entire universe.
Despite how powerful it was, nobody in the Nine Heavens sensed it—not even Cultivation Gods.
Yet that did not mean it went unnoticed. The Eternals who dwelled within the boundless void sensed it clearly, and it shook them more than the humans who sensed the second ripple.
When the ripple reached them, their bodies trembled uncontrollably. For many Eternals, it was the first time they had ever felt fear.
Those who had once tasted that emotion, however, needed no explanation. They instantly recognized its source.
Delight, awe, anticipation, fear, agitation, panic, dread, nervousness—an array of emotions surged through the Eternals. Yet among them all, fear and unease were the most dominant.
Of course, Yuan, the cause of all this, remained oblivious to the commotion he'd caused across the universe with his breakthrough into the God Ascension Realm.
"How long have I been cultivating...?" Yuan muttered to himself.
Though he had spent over two trillion years within the phenomenon, most of that experience faded upon returning to his body, as though it had all been a distant dream.
Yet one thing remained undeniable—his Soul Strength had grown tremendously, even if it was no longer as overwhelming as it had been during his ascension.
Before Yuan could gather his thoughts or examine his body, a brilliant light appeared at the end of the tunnel, its radiance cutting through and illuminating the void.
"Ah... finally..."
Yuan closed his eyes and embraced the light. Within moments, it enveloped his entire being.
As the gentle warmth dissolved, cool wind wrapped around him, caressing his skin like he was drifting—or perhaps falling—through the sky.

He snapped his eyes open, only to find himself plummeting from the sky toward a vast plain of crimson grass below. A minute later, his descent ended gracefully. As soon as his feet touched the ground, he began examining his surroundings.

chapters.title: Chapter 2358 Deprived Crimson Valley
paragraphs: As Yuan looked around, his gaze was met with a vast sea of crimson grass, its color disturbingly similar to dried blood. In the distance stood half-collapsed mountains, their jagged remains looming like silent witnesses to an ancient catastrophe.
The spiritual energy in the area was abundant and richer than anything he'd experienced in the Nine Heavens.
Yuan assumed he had arrived somewhere within the Nine Heavens, but his thoughts were suddenly interrupted by a sensation that made his brows knit tightly together.
It was an overwhelming foul smell—a stench so powerful that he was startled he hadn't noticed it sooner.
"Fuck!" Yuan cursed aloud, instinctively pinching his nose.
The smell was so bad that Yuan felt like he had fallen into an ocean of decomposing bodies.
Although he was shaken for a moment, Yuan quickly composed himself, and that's when he realized something.
"This smell... It's the same as that place... Did I—"
Yuan's thoughts were interrupted once again when several powerful presences suddenly emerged in the vicinity, surrounding him from every direction.
The presences were unmistakably those of God Ascension cultivators, but the killing intent radiating from them was wild and unrestrained—like rabid beasts that had not fed in ages.
"Food! It's food!"

"Hahaha! I can't believe there's food so deep in the Deprived Crimson Valley!" "And it's a lowly first-level False God!" Mere seconds after revealing their presence, three figures appeared before Yuan. Though they bore humanoid forms, they were anything but human—and Yuan recognized them instantly.
Crimson skin. Horns that protruded from their heads. And that unmistakable, foul stench they carried.
They were demons.
Not only were they demons, but they were all between the second and third level of God Ascension.
Despite facing three powerful demons, all with superior cultivation bases, Yuan remained calm, even speaking to them, "Did you just say the Deprived Crimson Valley?"
Instead of answering his question, they merely mocked him.
"You don't know where you are? Hahaha!"
"This idiot is so lost!"
Suddenly, a terrifying aura exploded from Yuan, but it was neither spiritual energy nor Celestial Qi.
Instead, overwhelming Demon Sealing Aura surged outward, descending upon the three demons like a crushing tidal wave.
The demons' movements froze in an instant, and a look of terror quickly washed over their faces. "T-This power!"

"This bastard is an Executioner!" "So what?! Not only is his cultivation weaker than ours, but there's only one of him against three of us!" After a brief moment of shock, the demons snapped out of their daze. Roaring in unison, they unleashed their own power and swiftly shattered the restraints binding them.
"Oh?" Yuan muttered with a somewhat surprised look.
Normally, Lower Demons like these crimson-skinned demons would not be able to resist his Demon Sealing Aura, regardless of their cultivation. Yet, they were able to do just that.
"Kill him before he tries anything else!" The demons quickly pounced toward Yuan simultaneously.
Seeing this, Yuan merely shook his head and muttered, "Demon Sealing Zone."
A small golden barrier suddenly materialized around Yuan, trapping the demons before they could even realize what had happened.
"I can't move my body!"
"What kind of technique is this?! I have never heard of anything like this before!" "What's happening to my body?! It feels like it's stiffening!"
"Y-Your body! It's turning into stone!"
"What?!"
"T-This can't be! He's not an Executioner, but a Sealer!"
"A Sealer?! That's impossible! They should no longer exist!"

"How else is he turning our bodies into stone?! This phenomenon only happens when a demon is being sealed!" Yuan observed their noisy outburst with mild amusement. Despite being demons, they lacked the mindless madness of the Lower Demons he had faced in the past.
"Hey!" One of the demons suddenly called out to Yuan. "Who the hell are you?! Are you really a Sealer?!"

"I will be the only one asking the questions here," Yuan calmly replied. "Now, answer my question. Is this place the Deprived Crimson Valley? If the next words that come out of your mouths don't answer my question, I'll completely seal you.
After a moment of silence, one of the demons responded, "That's right. This is the Deprived Crimson Valley—the Fourth Valley, to be exact."
Hearing this, Yuan rubbed his eyes and released a deep sigh.
Deprived Crimson Valley. Although he'd never visited this place, he had heard of its name before, so he knew where he'd been teleported.
However, there was one major problem.
The Deprived Crimson Valley did not exist within the Nine Heavens.
"There's no way..."
The foul stench thick in the air, the crimson expanse of the Deprived Crimson Valley, and the unusual Lower Demons before him left little room for doubt.
"Son of a bitch... How did I get teleported to the Demonic Realm?" Yuan sighed out loud.
Even though he didn't want to believe it, he couldn't ignore all of the evidence before him.
He had somehow entered the Demonic Realm... a forbidden domain that the Divine Paragon had personally sealed long ago.
With the entrance to the Demonic Realm sealed, there should have been no way for anyone to enter.
And yet, he had somehow done so. Through his own world, no less.

Of course, there was a chance that the seal had been undone. However, if that were the case, he would've been able to sense it, as the seal was directly connected to his soul. Though the mystery of his arrival weighed heavily on his mind, Yuan couldn't afford to contemplate it, as he had more pressing issues at hand.
He turned to look at the demons and asked, "You just said that Sealers no longer exist. Why did you say that?"
"Why? Isn't it obvious? They were all annihilated!"
"Seriously. Where did an ignorant bumpkin like you come from—" The demon hadn't even finished speaking when his body suddenly stiffened, then solidified into stone in an instant.
The other two demons stared at the sealed demon, their faces filled with horror.

chapters.title: Chapter 2359 The Demonic Realm
paragraphs: After sealing away one of the demons, Yuan calmly asked the remaining two, "Do you know of the name Divine Paragon?"
"Divine who?"
The demons looked at him with raised eyebrows, appearing genuinely puzzled by the name.
'How long has passed since I came here as Tian Chenyu?' Yuan wondered inwardly.
"What about the Demon Sealing Clan?" he continued to ask.
"Those bastards? They were annihilated many billions of years ago!" Yuan's eyes narrowed at this information.
"Who is the current Supreme Ruler?"
"That... we cannot tell you since the Supreme Ruler has changed several times, even before we were tossed into the Deprived Crimson Valley," said the demon.
"And we've been in here for at least a hundred million years."
Yuan pondered for a moment, trying to recall a certain name.
Then, he asked in a slow but clear voice, "Do you know of a demon named Dena?"
"D-Dena?" The two demons' expressions immediately twisted with surprise.

"Supreme Ruler Dena! Now that's a name I haven't heard in forever!" One of the demons laughed out loud. "You're lucky that you uttered that name while inside the Deprived Crimson Valley, you Sealer. Had you uttered that forbidden name outside of this place, you would've been slaughtered on sight," remarked the other demon.
Their words caused Yuan's eyebrows to raise with puzzlement.

Supreme Ruler Dena was one of the most powerful demons in the Demonic Realm, who ruled more than half of this realm when he visited as Tian Chenyu. How did such a powerful being become a forbidden subject, to the point where just uttering it would be a death sentence?
"What happened to her?" Yuan then asked.
"Seriously, where did you come from to not know even common sen—"
The demon who just spoke quickly covered his mouth after realizing his mistake.
"W-Wait! That was by accident—"
Without hesitation, Yuan sealed the demon.
Now, there was just one demon left.

Yuan turned to look at him, who swallowed nervously before responding, "Supreme Ruler Dena suddenly went crazy one day and went on a rampage, burning many cities to the ground and killing countless innocent people. Because of her actions, she was branded as a 'Forsaken' and exiled to the Deprived Crimson Valley."
"A Forsaken..." Yuan muttered.

It was a term he knew all too well. Only demons who had lost their reason—those unable to control their hunger and bloodlust—were given such a title. The Deprived Crimson Valley was where these Forsaken and criminals were exiled, abandoned, and left to be forgotten.
"So, Supreme Ruler Dena is currently in the Deprived Crimson Valley, huh?" he mumbled out loud to himself.

The demon nodded, "It's been several billion years since she was exiled, but it's not like anyone can execute that monster, so she should still be here. In the deepest part, the Final Valley, that is."
"Is there anything else you want to know? If not, I'd like you to release me. I swear I won't attack you again, and I am not a Forsaken, either."
Yuan glanced at him before asking, "Why were you exiled to this place?"

The demon suddenly fell silent as a heavy expression shaped his face. After a moment of silence, he spoke in a low voice, "My family was starving because of my lack of capabilities, so I stole some food as a desperate measure. Turns out I stole from the wrong bastard, and he executed my entire family in front of me as punishment. I went into a frenzy after witnessing that and attacked that bastard, who turned out to be a noble."
Yuan listened in silence, his expression blank.

"What about those two?" Yuan asked as his gaze darted between the two demons he'd sealed.
"They... they're also being punished for offending noble demons," he sighed.
"Is that so?" Just as Yuan was about to make his move, several more powerful presences flared into existence, rapidly closing in on their location.
Sensing this, Yuan let out a quiet sigh.
"I forgot... I need to completely mask my presence while I'm here..."
In an instant, Yuan activated Shadow Veil, his aura vanishing as though he had never existed.

Five demons appeared in just seconds, and they surrounded Yuan.
"Food! How long has it been since I last tasted meat?!"
Seeing this, the demon within Yuan's Demon Sealing Aura hastily warned them, "I wouldn't offend him if I were you! He's a Sealer!"
"Haha! Sealer?! What kind of nonsense is that? They're long gone!"
"Are you fucking blind?! Look at the two stone statues beside me!" The demons froze when they finally noticed the sealed demons, which they initially thought were just strangely shaped rocks.
Yet, despite the evidence right before their eyes, they refused to believe it.
Even though they had no explanation for the situation before them, these new demons were starving and couldn't care less. In the end, they all attacked Yuan.
Of course, Yuan, who was protected by the Demon Sealing Aura, instantly sealed the five of them.

The demon looked at him with a dumbfounded face.
"The Final Valley?! Are you trying to meet Supreme Ruler Dena? That's a death wish even for you!" he exclaimed.

chapters.title: Chapter 2360 The Demonic Realm(2)
paragraphs: "I don't know why you wish to meet Supreme Ruler Dena," the demon said, "but I strongly advise you against it."
Hearing a demon caution him about danger left Yuan momentarily speechless. He was not accustomed to such conversations with their kind, even with the Divine Paragon's memories.
"I appreciate your concern, but I need to meet her," Yuan calmly said.
The demon sighed before responding, "Alright, I'll tell you. But can you remove my restrictions? I cannot answer you even if I want to in my current state."
Without a word, Yuan removed the restraints on him.
The demon did a quick arm stretch before pointing south.
"If you travel in that direction, you will eventually arrive at the Final Valley."
"How far is it from here?" Yuan asked.
He knew the Deprived Crimson Valley was vast, but having never visited it—or paid much attention to it in his past life—he had no true understanding of just how immense it was.
"Well, I have never gone further than the Fifth Valley, so I cannot really say. However, just going from the Fourth Valley to the Fifth Valley will take you at least several years."
"Several years?!" Yuan exclaimed in shock.
After the initial shock subsided, Yuan suddenly recalled a crucial detail about the Demonic Realm.
'Oh, right... Just like the Primal Expanse, the flow of time here differs from that of the Nine Heavens.'
In fact, time in the Demonic Realm moved far faster than in the Nine Heavens—and even the accelerated flow within the Primal Expanse paled in comparison.
'What was it again? A year in this world is only a day in the Nine Heavens?' Yuan searched Tian Chenyu's memories to find this information.
If the disparity in time was truly this great, Yuan no longer felt concerned about spending several years in this place.
"How many valleys are there in the Deprived Crimson Valley?" Yuan asked.
"Ten in total," the demon replied. "The first nine are known as the First Valley through the Ninth Valley. The Final Valley lies at the very heart of this land."
"I see. Thank you for the information," Yuan said calmly as he began walking south.

"W-Wait!" the demon called out in a hesitant voice, pointing at the petrified figures. "What about them? Are you really going to leave them like that forever? This is my first time witnessing it, but according to legend, once a demon is sealed, they remain conscious—trapped in that state for eternity.

"That's correct." Yuan said indifferently." They're essentially buried alive for the remainder of their immortal lives. However, I didn't permanently seal them, so they'll return to normal after a few years."
"Is that so... Thank you for sparing us..."
Yuan stared at the demon for a moment before asking, "Hey, want to come with me?"
"Excuse me?" The demon's eyes widened at Yuan's abrupt question.
"I still have a lot of questions about this place, and it'd be nice to have someone to talk to while I travel to the Final Valley."
"Y-You might have a death wish, but I don't want to die yet! I still need to avenge my family!" The demon hastily refused, even though he might offend Yuan and risk being sealed.
"I can promise you that nothing will happen to you," Yuan calmly said, trying to persuade him.
"Also, how do you plan on taking revenge when you're stuck in this place for the rest of your life?"
"T-That's..." The demon fell silent.

Once a demon is exiled to the Deprived Crimson Valley, leaving is virtually impossible. Those cast here are condemned to remain for the rest of their lives. Yet with lifespans that border on eternity, their only true release is death.
In that sense, they were not so different from Yu Ning and Ji Ran, who were once trapped within the Shadow Realm, fated to wither away in isolation or consumed by other souls.
"It's not completely impossible to leave this place," the demon said, a flicker of hope in his eyes. "I've heard that some exiles have managed to regain their freedom before."
Yuan chuckled softly. "Perhaps a few fortunate ones were freed under special circumstances. But do you truly believe such luck will fall upon you?"
The demon fell silent.
After a brief pause, Yuan added, "Follow me. Keep me entertained, and I'll help you leave this place."
The demon swallowed nervously at Yuan's tempting offer.
"How will you free me?" he asked.
However, the demon's jaw dropped when Yuan shrugged his shoulders and replied, "I have no idea right now, but I'll figure a way. I promise.
"Seriously...?" The demon sighed out loud.

Despite Yuan's lousy response, the demon could not ignore the unwavering confidence in his voice. More than that, there was something about Yuan—an indescribable presence—that made him seem strangely trustworthy.
Without waiting for a reply, Yuan turned around and began walking away.
"If you don't wish to follow me, then don't," he said over his shoulder. "I won't force you. You're free to remain here for the rest of your life—clinging to a revenge that will never come."
When the demon heard such words, he felt something snap inside his head.
Then, without even realizing it, he started moving toward Yuan.
"I... I will come with you!" he declared.
"What's your name?" Yuan then asked. "I'm Yuan."
"You can just call me Lev."
"Let's go, Lev. Try not to fall behind."
Yuan suddenly leaped into the sky. In the next instant, beautiful flames erupted around him, forming a pair of fiery wings on his back as he shot forward like a flaming meteor.
"What the heck?!" Lev exclaimed, stunned by Yuan's movement technique.
But when he saw how quickly Yuan was vanishing into the horizon, he swallowed his shock and hurriedly gave chase.
Meanwhile, somewhere within the Ninth Heaven, those connected to Yuan—such as Feng Yuxiang and Xiao Hua—suddenly felt their bond with him severed.
"This feeling... Young Master?!"
"Yuan?!"
The moment their connection with Yuan was severed, Feng Yuxiang, Xiao Hua, and Lan Yingying immediately halted whatever they were doing.

chapters.title: Chapter 2361 Qian Chu's Return
paragraphs: Although they were startled when their connection with Yuan was suddenly severed, it wasn't the first time they had experienced such a situation, so they did not immediately panic as they had before, choosing instead to calmly consider the possible reasons.

'The last time my connection with the Young Master severed like this, he was thrown into the Primal Expanse, but he should be doing the trial within the Stairway to Heaven... or did he finish?' Feng Yuxiang pondered inwardly.

'The Stairway to Heaven disappeared not long ago and hasn't returned since, so maybe it took the Young Master to some place that's so far away that it severed our connection. Knowing the Young Master, he'll most likely be fine...'
"What's the matter?" Yingzi asked Feng Yuxiang after noticing that she'd abruptly stopped moving.
"The Young Master's trying to worry us like usual, but I won't fall for it this time!" Feng Yuxiang remarked with a resolute face.
"Yuan? What happened to him?" Yingzi asked with an intrigued face.
"I don't know, and there's nothing we can really do about it now but trust in him. He definitely wouldn't want us to worry, that I am sure."
"Alright. Then let's get back to training."
Meanwhile, Xiao Hua, Lingyue, and Lan Yingying had a similar conversation.
"Knowing Yuan, he's probably doing something crazy again," Xiao Hua sighed out loud.
"Unless he's fighting an Eternal, we don't need to worry about him at all," Lan Yingying chuckled.

"Brother Yuan will definitely be fine. Let's focus on improving ourselves so that when he returns, we can surprise him," Lingyue said calmly as she flicked her arm, sending the blood coating her hands splattering onto the green grass below.
At her feet lay a massive magical beast, its enormous body motionless. Though it no longer breathed, the lingering aura of a True Immortal still clung to its corpse.
"Un." Both Xiao Hua and Lan Yingying nodded.
Lan Yingying, who was in her beast form, opened her mouth and proceeded to consume the magical beast, causing her aura to soar.

At the same time, the rest of the Nine Heavens were in a wary state—particularly the Demon Sealing Clan and the Demon Sealing Grotto. In recent times, the activities of the Demon Worshippers and demons had increased at an alarming rate, swamping the Demon Sealers with work.

However, with demons having been absent for so many years, the Demon Sealers lacked real combat experience. It didn't take long for them to realize how much they had declined—needing large groups just to handle a single Lower Demon.

Thankfully, the Demon Sealing Grotto wasn't as helpless. Founded by a previous generation of formidable Demon Sealers with stricter requirements, it had a far stronger foundation. Moreover, under Yan Hara's guidance, their strength had only continued to grow.
Somewhere in the Nine Heavens, a certain figure sat before an army of demons.
'It's been over twenty years, but I haven't heard a peep from that bastard since then... Did he forget about our deal... or is he up to something?'
Qian Chu wondered to himself as he gazed at the three Demon Sealing Treasures before him.
'Well, it doesn't matter. The Demon Sealing Treasures are already in my possession, and it will only be a matter of time before I reopen the Demonic Realm!'
"Master!" A demon suddenly approached Qian Chu and bowed before him.
"What is it?"

"Our plans to weaken the Demon Sealing Clan are not proceeding smoothly. Although most of their Demon Sealers are weak, they have a few exceptionally powerful ones, especially that woman named Yan Hara, who received the Divine Paragon's legacy."
"Yan Hara, huh?" Qian Chu's gaze narrowed at the Demon Sealing Flag, recalling the incident where it saved her on its own accord.
"I don't know how she acquired the Divine Paragon's legacy, but she won't be enough to stop us.
Qian Chu stood up and said, "Anyways, it's about time that I returned to the Demon Sealing Clan. As for Yan Hara... I'll deal with her myself."
He turned to face the army of demons and said, "Continue weakening the Demon Sealing Clan and the Demon Sealing Grotto as planned. We will open the Demonic Realm within the next ten years!"
"Yes, Master!" The army of demons roared with excitement.
Meanwhile, within the Demon Sealing Clan, Yan Hara continued expanding her influence.

The surge in demonic activity provided her with ample opportunity to display her abilities. Time and again, she stepped forward to save the lives of fellow Demon Sealers, causing her reputation—and authority—to soar. Qian Chu's prolonged absence only further advanced her ambitions.

Unfortunately for her, seizing his position was far from simple. Qian Chu had spent thousands of years consolidating his authority within the clan, and over that time, he had planted numerous loyalists and spies throughout its ranks.
"Senior Yan! Did you hear? The Clan Leader, Qian Chu, has announced his return to the Demon Sealing Clan and will return by the end of the month!"
Yan Hara nodded with a serious expression on her face. Although she was nervous about Qian Chu's return, she expected it to happen eventually. "Is it finally time for us to clash?" she muttered.
Despite her immense progress within the Demon Sealing Clan, she realized that unless she defeated Qian Chu, she would never claim his position as the Clan Leader.

After a moment of silence, Yan Hara faced the group of Demon Sealers before her and declared, "The time to kick Qian Chu, the traitor, off his throne is near. Have all of our Elite Demon Sealers and above return to prepare for the battle."
"Yes!"
As the Demon Sealers left, leaving Yan Hara alone, she lifted her head and stared at the sky with a dazed face and mumbled, "Where are you... Yuan?"
Back at the Deprived Crimson Valley, Yuan and Lev had been traveling for nearly four years without rest.
"I can see it! The Fifth Valley is just ahead!" Lev exclaimed when he saw a certain mountain on the horizon.
